This assembly is my best reading of the geometry. I could not test it, and a few placements are guesses.

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1376 768">
  <use href="#kit-base_plate" transform="translate(543,657)"/>
  <use href="#kit-pump_body" transform="translate(688,323) rotate(70) translate(-35.6,-92.6)"/>
  <use href="#kit-spout" transform="translate(627,430) rotate(235) translate(-60,-278.2)"/>
  <use href="#kit-piston_rod" transform="translate(688,166.3) rotate(-70) translate(-315.8,-25.4)"/>
  <use href="#kit-cap" transform="translate(762,329) rotate(180)"/>
  <use href="#kit-handle_lever" transform="translate(632.3,102.8) rotate(130) translate(-173.34,-130.2)"/>
  <use href="#kit-link_bar" transform="translate(801.1,57.4) rotate(46.9) translate(-27.97,-27.81)"/>
</svg>
```

- **Base plate:** it stays upright and unrotated, placed so the pedestal is centred on x = 688 and the ground line is at y = 745.
- **Pump body:** I stood it vertically with the bore chamber at the top and the wider chamber at the bottom, so its bottom plate sits flat on the pedestal.
- **Cap:** I rotated it 180° so the cap stands on the body top on its flat base. The fulcrum lug with the two holes is then up and to the left of the body axis.
- **Handle lever:** I pinned the lever's middle hole (the one inside the arm) to the upper of the two cap holes. The long arm points left, and the short-arm end hole is up and to the right of the body axis. The lever angle is a choice, not something the parts fix.
- **Link bar:** it joins the lever's end hole to the piston rod's top hole.
- **Piston rod:** it hangs vertically on the body centre line, with its head inside the bore.
- **Spout:** I rotated it so its flange sits flat against the left wall of the bore chamber and the nozzle points downward.

Three points are guesses:
- **Fulcrum choice:** I picked the upper cap hole and the lever's middle hole as the fulcrum pair over the alternatives.
- **Spout height:** I placed the flange at the middle of the bore chamber.
- **Cap seat:** I took the seat as the centre of the cap's flat base.
